text.p: Shanghai's third elevated highway linking its airport to the main ring road around the city centre has opened for traffic, the Liberation Daily reported on Tuesday.
The 6.2-km highway runs from Hongqiao airport in the west of the city eastwards to the elevated ring road. It is operated as a toll road with automobiles charged 15 yuan and motorcycles five yuan.
Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, a Hong Kong-listed company majority owned by the Shanghai city government, owns 50.2 percent of the highway.

The highway will have a total length of 8.8 km on its completion at the end of 1997, with an additional 2.6 km running from the ring road to the Huangpu river to the east of the city centre, the China Securities newspaper said on Tuesday.
Shanghai Industrial expects an annual profit of 14-15 percent from the road, the newspaper said.
Another elevated highway runs north-south over the city centre.
The highway network is aimed at relieving serious traffic congestion in the Shanghai city area.
